items.abstract: <jats:p>The combination of tree structure search and reinforcement learning reasoning process is a reinforcement learning method by introducing intermediate steps into the reasoning tree to achieve no additional introduction of reward model conditions. This method reduces the risk of credit distribution and reward deception to a certain extent. This paper systematically reviews and analyzes the research direction of strong chemistry combined with tree structure search to improve the reasoning ability of large language models. After conducting relevant research, this paper focuses on two issues: whether the tree search mechanism actually changes the reasoning structure of the language model. This method is difficult at the level of computational cost and scalability. Comprehensive research shows that the core value of the combination of tree structure search and reinforcement learning is to transform the reasoning process from linear generation to a more complex structured decision problem, which gives more intensive process signals for reinforcement learning, but the performance improvement still depends on the basic model's ability and search budget control.</jats:p>
title: Reinforcement Learning Combined with Tree Structure Search Enhances the Reasoning Ability of Large Language Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>Optimizing patent claims is a critical yet challenging task, demanding careful balance between maximizing novelty and preserving legal scope. Manual claim drafting is labor-intensive, costly, and inherently inconsistent, while conventional Large Language Models (LLMs) often lack the structured, iterative reasoning essential for precise claim refinement. To address these challenges, we introduce Tree of Claims (ToC), an innovative framework that redefines claim editing as a guided search problem. ToC synergistically integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with a collaborative multi-agent system, comprising an LLM-based EditorAgent that proposes contextually grounded edits, and an ExaminerAgent that mimics patent examiner critiques through structured, chain-of-thought analyses of novelty and prior art disclosure. Driven by a carefully designed multi-objective reward function, ToC jointly optimizes novelty, scope retention, and semantic coherence. Experimental evaluation on a benchmark of 1145 claims demonstrates that ToC significantly outperforms standard LLMs in zero-shot and few-shot scenarios, achieving an average composite score improvement of 8%, and up to 9% in certain cases. Extensive experiments, including detailed ablation studies, validate ToC’s efficacy in generating superior, legally robust claim revisions. Overall, ToC establishes a transparent, controllable, and interpretable methodology that effectively bridges advanced LLM reasoning capabilities with strategic MCTS planning for structured patent claim optimization.</jats:p>
title: ToC: Tree-of-Claims Search with Multi-Agent Language Models

items.abstract: Solving grade-school math problems is a challenging task for small, open-source language models because of their limited step-by-step reasoning and the tendency to spread calculation mistakes. This limitation is partly attributed to their inclination to reproduce patterns seen during training rather than performing genuine reasoning. We present a two-round reinforcement learning framework in which a fine-tuned Gemma-7B-it–based evaluator dynamically scores both the reasoning and final answers and gives back corrective hints. A Gemma-2B-it generator is then optimized via PPO, utilizing these per-example rewards and hints to iteratively enhance its outputs. On a reserved test subset of the GSM8K, our approach achieves an accuracy of 8.36% in answer accuracy with the PPO trained Gemma-2B-it, and 9.23% when we add a dynamic evaluator in test time.
title: Enhancing Math Reasoning in Small Language Models via Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Agent Evaluation Feedback
